description: The bar chart compares the accuracy of different models on paraphrase sentiment and STS tasks. The vertical axis represents accuracy or correlation, ranging from 0 to 0.8, with a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists five different models: Single-task baseline, Baseline with Adaptive Dropout, Unsupervised SimCSE, Supervised SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE. Each model is represented by a group of three bars, each bar corresponding to a different task: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue). The Single-task baseline model has the lowest accuracy across all tasks, with values around 0.4 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.5 for STS Correlation, and 0.6 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The Baseline with Adaptive Dropout model shows improved accuracy, with values around 0.6 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.7 for STS Correlation, and 0.7 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The Unsupervised SimCSE model has similar accuracy to the Baseline with Adaptive Dropout, with values around 0.6 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.7 for STS Correlation, and 0.7 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The Supervised SimCSE model shows the highest accuracy, with values around 0.7 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.8 for STS Correlation, and 0.8 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The 2-Tier SimCSE model has the highest accuracy, with values around 0.8 for Sentiment Accuracy, 0.8 for STS Correlation, and 0.8 for Paraphrase Accuracy. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, and no bars are visually emphasized.
